## The unit-vector connection {#iv6-unit-vectors .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson}

```{=html}
<p>For non-zero vectors, it can be shown that</p>
<div class="a-eq a-unit-factor"><span data-math="\frac{1}{|\underset{\sim}{a}|}\bigl(\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}\bigr)=\hat{\underset{\sim}{a}}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}"></span>.</div>
<p class="a-extension-note">We will prove this using the algebraic properties of the scalar product in <strong>Extension 2</strong>.</p>
<div class="a-unit-equivalence"><p>The cosine formula can therefore be written equivalently as</p>
<div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\boxed{\cos\theta=\frac{\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}}{|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|}=\hat{\underset{\sim}{a}}\cdot\hat{\underset{\sim}{b}}}"></span></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 41</div>

::: notes
State the scalar-factor identity without proving the algebraic laws here; students will study these in Extension 2. Applying the same idea to both non-zero vectors gives (a·b)/(|a||b|)=â·b̂. Emphasise that the dot product of the unit vectors equals cos theta, not theta. No geometric normalisation derivation is needed on this slide.
:::
